problem: Embodied household-task agents are trained and evaluated in clean simulators, and ablations do not directly test how robust each sensory modality is to real-world environmental changes such as low light, glass doors or mirrors.
motivation: Assistive care robots for the elderly must work in varied homes where lighting fails or new glass doors and mirrors appear. Models that rely on one modality (vision) may fail while others (depth, maps) might cope. It is unclear which modalities carry task success, so the authors propose testing them directly with controlled disturbances.
key_idea: Define 'disturbances' (dimmed light, glass door/wall, mirror) that disable or corrupt specific modalities in AI2Thor ALFRED scenes and measure how existing agents (FILM, HLSM, EmBERT) degrade.
insight: A glass wall lowers goal-condition success for both models, and HLSM suffers more (GC 44.02 to 26.13) than FILM (39.41 to 31.28). Giving HLSM ground-truth depth partly recovers performance in glass-wall scenes (SR 12.50, GC 35.36), which suggests depth is the modality that matters for transparent obstacles. Qualitatively, agents get stuck bumping into the wall and hit the 10-failed-action limit, while FILM's semantic map sometimes registers the wall as an obstacle. These are preliminary results on few episodes, so the conclusions are tentative.
method: Disturbance definition: any external change in the environment that limits or disables properties of one or more modalities, forcing generalisation to unseen conditions.
Disturbance set: dimmed light (bright to none), glass door/wall blocking movement, and mirror giving redundant or misleading visual information (mirror still planned).
Task selection: 6 ALFRED tests_seen tasks on a single floorplan, each with 3 goal-instruction pairs, chosen so the disturbance matters and the models can solve the task undisturbed.
Episode extension: 3 extra random agent start positions added, giving 4 starts x 3 instructions x 6 tasks = 72 episodes per condition.
Models: open-source ALFRED agents HLSM, FILM and EmBERT (only FILM and HLSM tested so far).
Metrics: Task Success rate and Goal Condition success, with sub-goals verified manually.

numbers_note: Preliminary work-in-progress; only FILM and HLSM under one disturbance (glass wall) were evaluated. The split is described as ALFRED tests_seen restricted to one floorplan.
results: A glass wall reduces goal-condition success for both models: FILM 39.41 to 31.28 with unchanged SR (16.67), HLSM 44.02 to 26.13 with SR 15.28 to 8.33. HLSM is affected more, and GT depth partially restores it (SR 12.50, GC 35.36).
limitations: Very small preliminary evaluation (6 tasks, 72 episodes, one disturbance, two models), so differences are not statistically meaningful.
Mirror and dimmed-light disturbances and EmBERT are not yet evaluated.
Simulation only, on seen floorplans with low baseline success (~15-17%), which limits measurable effect.
